statement: A tree is given as: a line with n, then a line of n level-order entries where -1 marks an absent child; each placed node consumes the next two entries as its children. Print yes when the tree is a valid BST - at every node, the entire left subtree is smaller and the entire right subtree larger - and no otherwise. Pass an allowed interval down: the root gets an unbounded one, a left child lowers the ceiling to the parent's value, a right child raises the floor. Checking only parent against children is the classic trap.
constraints: Values are positive and distinct; -1 marks an absent child.

example.why: Every node respects every ancestor turn; equivalently, inorder prints 2 5 7 8 12 14, strictly increasing.

hint: Either carry (low, high) ranges down, or inorder-walk and verify strictly increasing output.
mistake: Comparing each node with its children only - a deep 9 under root 8 passes locally and breaks globally.
